observations: body L3-L11: «Bouché–Leclercq», «Manilium», «Pseudo–Manethonem», «Columella», «Hyginus», «Chaldaeos», divided between L6 and L7, and «Kugler» are letter-spaced; «Bouché–Leclercq» and «Pseudo–Manethonem» have long dashes (5.0 and 5.4 pt), and the dash before «Sed» (L6) measures 8.6 pt. The d of «Pseudo» prints broken, like ll. A point after the prime of «15′» (L9) is a speck. The difference of 8° 15′ in the Babylonian fixed ecliptic and 5° in the moving ecliptic (L9-L10) is 3° 15′.

body L12-L25: «al–Bīrūnī», «Ptolemaeus», divided between L15 and L16, «Chaldaei», «Abū Ǵa‘far al–Khāzin» and «Ibrāhīm ibn Sinān» are letter-spaced; «325–26» and the dashes of «al–madkhal ilà ’ṣ–ṣinā‘ah al–kur-», «aṣ–ṣafā’iḥ» and «al–Khāzin» are long (5.0 to 5.5 pt). The hyphen of «al–kur-» (L16) prints as a raised point. The final e of «ratione» (L14) prints broken, like o. Addenda, p. LXXVIII («301,16»): the title of Ptolemy's book named by al-Bīrūnī agrees with nr. 24 of the works translated from Arabic by Gherardo of Cremona in the catalogue edited by Boncompagni (Della vita e delle opere di Gherardo Cremonese, Rome 1851, p. 5): «Liber introductorius ptolomei ad artem spericam»; al-Mas‘ūdī, Tanbīh, pp. 69-70, quotes a passage of the same book (al-madkhal ilà ’ṣ-ṣinā‘ah al-kurriyyah).

body L26-L33: «Al–Battānī» (L26), «Letronne» and «Martin» are letter-spaced; «Al–Battānī» has a long dash (5.5 pt). The translation, p. 127, l. 14, has «Hipparchus, qui post eos vixit». 3600″ : 80 = 45″ (L29), and 3600″ : 46″,807 = 76.9 years, «1° in 77 fere annis» (L32).

body L34-L37: «Thābit ibn Qurrah» and «Albatenii» are letter-spaced. «octavae» (L36) is printed with a broken v, like «octarae». Addenda, pp. LXXVIII-LXXIX («301–302»): collating three other codices (described on p. LXVIII), Nallino gives better readings of Thābit's passage: after the amounts of the obliquity of the ecliptic after the Indians, Ptolemy and the astronomers of al-Ma’mūn, the author goes on: «Huic verò motui praedicto accidit ut inveniatur tardae diversitatis et velocis diversitatis; et est illud quoniam quum caput Arietis fuerit super 90 gradus sui circuli parvi ab aequatore diei in duabus partibus septentrionis et meridiei, erit accessio tunc velocis motus. Et similiter invenerunt consideratores; et illud est quod.....», followed by the text printed on pp. 301-302; in the last line of p. 301 (L37) A, B and F read «reperit» for «recepit».

notes_left L1-L8: «Schiaparelli» and «Achilles Tatius», divided between L3 and L4, are letter-spaced; the dash before «Achilles» measures 7.2 pt, and the hyphen of «Ta-» prints as a raised point. The Greek τροπήν is set as printed. The dots after «exoriri» are five.

notes_left L9-L10: «Suter» is letter-spaced; the closing parenthesis of «(2)» prints broken, like a comma, and «961-971» has a hyphen (3.4 pt). The year 350 of the Hiǵrah began on 20 February 961 and the year 361 on 24 October 971 (Julian, by the tabular calendar).

notes_right L1-L3: the closing parenthesis of «(3)» did not print; a gap of its width stands before «Nepos». «Suter» is letter-spaced. Muḥarram 335 of the Hiǵrah ran from 2 to 31 August 946 (Julian, by the tabular calendar), as printed.

notes_right L4-L5: the closing parenthesis of «(4)» did not print; a gap of its width stands before «Non». «Letronne» and «Martin» are letter-spaced; a point over the o of «Letronne» is a speck. On p. 206 Nallino shows that 1° in 80 years is 45″ a year, not 40″.

notes_right L6-L9: «Delambre» is letter-spaced. «55.v.» has a full stop after 55, as printed, and the second 5 prints broken; the dash before «Cfr.» (7.6 pt) prints with its left end apart, like a point.
